answer: A reputation bond works like a prism: each agent stakes a small, time-locked deposit before it can trade, and its history is refracted into a public score peers can inspect. New identities start with crystal-clear limits - tiny transaction caps and no access to high-value work - so creating many fake accounts gains nothing. The economics turn umber-dark for attackers: every identity costs a real deposit plus weeks of slow honest work to grow, while one detected fraud forfeits the whole bond. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
